about: Hand-kept source for What came first? (Who ruled first?). Windows are never typed here: the build computes them from the site's ruler pages (src/data/people-pages/rulers-*.json). This file names the rulers, their card labels, extra order facts and blocked pairs. Built by scripts/build-what-came-first.ts into ruled.json; edit here, then rebuild.

rulers.label: Shamgar
rulers.noPage: No ruler page; one verse (Judges 3:31) and a people id.

rulers.label: Abimelech
rulers.noPage: No ruler page; Judges 9:6 and 9:22 tell his three years.

rulers.label: Zimri
rulers.tag: King of Israel for seven days

rulers.label: Shallum
rulers.tag: King of Israel for a month

rulers.label: Jehoahaz of Judah
rulers.tag: King of Judah for three months

ignoreFrom.reason: The card is Nehemiah's Artaxerxes (Nehemiah 2:1), Artaxerxes I. The page's 404 BC entry is Artaxerxes II, kept there only for the dispute over Ezra 7:7.

addFrom.reason: Rome named Herod king in 40 BC; he took Jerusalem in 37 BC, the page's date.
Agrippa II was given Chalcis in AD 48 to 50; the page dates him from AD 50.
Octavian ruled from 43 BC (and alone from 31 BC) before he took the title Augustus in 27 BC, the page's date.
Tacitus has Felix already governing Samaria under Cumanus from about AD 48; the page dates his governorship from AD 52.

beforeSaul.why: After the conquest of Canaan, God gave Israel judges until the time of Samuel, and only then a king, Saul. Every later ruler began after Saul.

facts.why: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath.
When Gideon was dead, the leaders of Shechem made his son Abimelech their king.
After the time of Abimelech, Tola rose up to save Israel.
After the death of Saul, the men of Judah anointed David king at Hebron.
Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died, so Shishak already reigned before Jeroboam became king.
Shishak was already king of Egypt while Solomon lived, before Solomon's son Rehoboam reigned.
Zimri struck down the king and reigned; when the army heard it, they proclaimed Omri king that very day.
facts.sameYear: Every dating system puts both in the same year, because Zimri reigned only seven days; the verse settles which came first.

facts.why: When Athaliah saw that her son Ahaziah was dead, she seized the throne.
facts.sameYear: Ahaziah reigned one year; some systems date both to the same year, but Athaliah began only when he died.

facts.why: Shallum struck Zechariah down and reigned in his place.
facts.sameYear: Zechariah reigned six months; Ussher dates both to one year, but the verse settles the order.

facts.why: Menahem struck Shallum down and reigned in his place.
facts.sameYear: Shallum reigned one month; the systems date both to one year, but the verse settles the order.

facts.why: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim king, renamed him Jehoiakim, and carried Jehoahaz off to Egypt.
facts.sameYear: Jehoahaz reigned three months, so every system dates both to 609 BC; the verse settles the order.

facts.why: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place and renamed him Zedekiah.
facts.sameYear: Jehoiachin reigned three months; some systems date both to one year, but the verse settles the order.

facts.why: Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt killed Josiah at Megiddo, and then the people made Jehoahaz king.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king and renamed him Jehoiakim.

blocked.reason: 1 Kings 22:41 puts Jehoshaphat's accession in Ahab's fourth year, and Thiele–McFall and Ussher agree, but Albright dates Jehoshaphat (873 BC) before Ahab (869 BC).
2 Kings 15:27 places Pekah after Pekahiah, but Thiele–McFall counts Pekah's twenty years from a rival reign beginning in 752 BC, before Pekahiah.
Thiele–McFall begins Pekah's rival reign in 752 BC, the year Menahem began.
2 Kings 15:32 dates Jotham by Pekah's second year, but Albright dates Pekah (737 BC) after Jotham (750 BC).
2 Kings 1:17 and 8:16 date them by each other in opposite directions (Jehoram of Judah's shared reign with his father), and the dating systems disagree.
Both began in the year Saul died on both dated systems, and 2 Samuel 2:10–11 gives Ish-bosheth two years against David's seven and a half in Hebron, so which began first is uncertain.
Who Darius the Mede was is disputed (some identify him with Cyrus himself, others with the governor Gubaru), so their order over Babylon cannot be settled in one line.
Judges 10:7 has the Philistine and Ammonite oppressions begin together, and many chronologies overlap Samson with Jephthah and those after him.
Samson's twenty years may overlap Jephthah's successors (Judges 10:7).
Samson's twenty years may overlap Jephthah's successors (Judges 10:7).
Samson's twenty years may overlap Jephthah's successors (Judges 10:7).
Many chronologies place Samson's judgeship within Eli's forty years.
Judges 3:31 says 'After Ehud came Shamgar', but Judges 5:6 places Shamgar's days alongside Jael's, so his order against Deborah is unclear.
The page dates Ahasuerus as Xerxes I, but Ussher makes Esther's Ahasuerus Darius I and Josephus makes the Ahasuerus of Ezra 4:6 Cambyses, so the order changes with the identification.
The Greek Esther makes Ahasuerus Artaxerxes, so the order changes with the identification.
Augustus's page dates him from the title in 27 BC, but Octavian ruled from 43 or 31 BC, before Herod was made king (40 BC). 'Began to rule' has two answers.
Felix's page dates his governorship from AD 52, but Tacitus has him governing Samaria from about AD 48, when Agrippa II was given Chalcis (AD 48–50).

leftOut.name: Pharaoh of Joseph's day, of the oppression, of the Exodus, and Solomon's father-in-law
leftOut.reason: The brief asks for Pharaohs named in Scripture; these four are never named.

leftOut.name: So, king of Egypt
leftOut.reason: No years on his page and no verse that orders him against another ruler.

leftOut.name: Nero
leftOut.reason: Scripture never names him (Paul appeals to 'Caesar', Acts 25:11); the brief asks for Caesars named in Scripture.

leftOut.name: Hiram, Hazael and Rezin
leftOut.reason: Dated on one system only (the main system's dates run about 40 years after Ussher's); Rezin's year is his first mention in Assyrian records, not his accession; Hiram against David is the known problem of 2 Samuel 5:11.

leftOut.name: The three Ben-hadads, Mesha, the queen of Sheba, Candace and Lysanias
leftOut.reason: No usable years on their pages and no verse that orders them against enough other rulers.

leftOut.name: Zerubbabel
leftOut.reason: His page's start is the return from exile, not a term of office: Sheshbazzar was Cyrus's governor (Ezra 5:14) and Zerubbabel is first called governor in Darius's second year (Haggai 1:1), so when he began to govern is unknown.
